observation.visible_scene: Close-up of a black handheld payment terminal (POS device) resting on a dark, glossy reflective countertop. The terminal's angled keypad with red, yellow and green function keys and a small blank screen faces the viewer. A person's right hand grips the rear/side of the terminal, holding it steady. The background is dim and heavily out of focus, with a small blue light at the far left. The terminal's reflection is visible on the surface beneath it.
visible_changes: From t=0.0s to about t=1.6s the shot is essentially static: the terminal, its reflection, the holding right hand, and the blurred background all remain in fixed positions.
Around t=1.68s the index finger of a left hand begins to enter the frame from the left edge.
Over t=1.76s–t=3.2s that left index finger moves rightward and slightly downward, extending toward the terminal's keypad.
By the end of the excerpt the fingertip hovers directly over the upper keypad area near the colored/function keys, in a pressing/reaching pose.
The right hand and the terminal itself stay largely stationary throughout the whole clip; the only clear motion is the incoming left finger.
The background and reflection show no independent movement, indicating the camera is static.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the finger actually depresses a key or merely hovers (the clip ends before any definitive contact result).
Any change to the terminal's screen or any transaction outcome after this segment.
How the terminal and the holding hand got into position before t=0.
Whether the two hands belong to one person or to two different people (only hands are visible).
uncertain_details: The exact key being targeted is unclear because the fingertip overlaps the keypad edge and the colored-button row; contact vs. hover cannot be confirmed from the frames.
The motion is slow and small, so the finger's trajectory is read from its changing position relative to the fixed terminal rather than from large displacement.
Sub-pixel camera drift cannot be fully ruled out, but the constant background blur and stable reflection support a static camera.

may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
